topics.title: Tiling and the exact meaning of a quadrilateral

learn.hook: Floor tiles fit with no gaps and no overlaps. Which four-sided shapes can do that? Every parallelogram, for a start!
points: A tiling covers the plane with copies of a shape with no gaps and no overlaps.
Any parallelogram tiles the plane: two sets of equally spaced parallel lines (like sticks pinned in a grid) make rows of identical parallelograms.
A quadrilateral ABCD is made from four points A, B, C, D (no three on a line) and the four segments AB, BC, CD, DA, where the segments meet only at their ends.
A, B, C, D are vertices; AB, BC, CD, DA are sides; AC and BD are diagonals. AB and BC are adjacent sides; AB and CD are opposite sides; A and C are opposite vertices; ∠A and ∠C are opposite angles.
Name a quadrilateral by going round it in order: ABCD, BCDA or DCBA all name the same one, but ABDC is a different figure.

example.q: For quadrilateral PQRS, list the diagonals, a pair of opposite sides and the angle opposite ∠Q.
steps: Diagonals join opposite vertices: PR and QS
Opposite sides: PQ and RS (also QR and SP)

learn.reallife: Brick walls, chessboards and floor tiles are all tilings by parallelograms (rectangles and squares).

games.title: Naming rules
items: ABCD and CDAB name the same quadrilateral.
Both go round in the same order from a different start.
ABCD and ABDC always name the same quadrilateral.
ABDC joins B to D as a side, a different figure.
In ABCD, ∠A and ∠C are opposite angles.
A and C are opposite vertices.
AB and BC are opposite sides.
They share B, so they are adjacent.
Every parallelogram can tile the plane.
Rows of translated copies fill the plane.

quiz.q: What does a tiling of the plane require?
options: Copies of shapes that cover it with no gaps and no overlaps
quiz.explain: Gaps or overlaps are not allowed in a tiling.
steps: A tiling covers the plane with copies of a shape.
There must be no gaps and no overlaps.
Answer: Copies of shapes that cover it with no gaps and no overlaps
quiz.mistake: Thinks tiles may overlap

quiz.q: Which shape can always tile the plane?
quiz.explain: Translating a parallelogram along its two side directions fills the plane.
steps: Two sets of equally spaced parallel lines make rows of identical parallelograms.
So any parallelogram tiles the plane.
Circles leave gaps; regular pentagons and octagons do not fit around a point.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only squares can tile

quiz.q: In quadrilateral WXYZ, which segment is a diagonal?
quiz.explain: A diagonal joins opposite (non-adjacent) vertices.
steps: WX, YZ, ZW are sides; W and Y are opposite.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a side with a diagonal

quiz.q: In quadrilateral ABCD, which side is opposite to BC?
quiz.explain: BC and DA share no vertex.
steps: BC uses B and C; DA uses D and A.
quiz.mistake: Picks an adjacent side

quiz.q: Which name describes the same quadrilateral as ABCD?
quiz.explain: DCBA goes round the same vertices in reverse order.
steps: The name must go round the vertices in order.
DCBA goes round A, B, C, D in reverse: the same quadrilateral.
ACBD, ABDC, BACD change the order of joining.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any order of the four letters is fine

quiz.q: Why do we need 'no three of the four points on a line' in the definition?
options: Otherwise two sides would lie along one line and it would collapse into a triangle
So that it has a right angle
quiz.explain: Three collinear points would make a straight angle, not a true corner.
steps: If three points were on a line, two sides would lie along one line.
That corner would be a straight angle, and the shape would collapse to a triangle.
Answer: Otherwise two sides would lie along one line and it would collapse into a triangle
quiz.mistake: Ignores the need for genuine corners

quiz.q: How many diagonals does a quadrilateral have?
quiz.explain: AC and BD.
steps: Diagonals join opposite vertices: A to C and B to D.
quiz.mistake: Counts sides

quiz.q: In quadrilateral ABCD, which pair are adjacent angles?
quiz.explain: A and B are joined by side AB.
steps: Adjacent angles are at the ends of one side.
quiz.mistake: Picks opposite angles

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "What exactly is a quadrilateral, and what is a diagonal?"
teach.praise: Great! Four points joined in order by four sides, and diagonals join opposite vertices!
teach.nudge: How many points and segments are there? What does a diagonal connect?

revise.summary: A tiling covers the plane with no gaps or overlaps; any parallelogram tiles. A quadrilateral ABCD is four points (no three collinear) joined in order by four sides that meet only at their ends.
focus: Identify sides, diagonals, opposite and adjacent parts.
Name quadrilaterals correctly.
Explain why parallelograms tile.
remember: Diagonals join opposite vertices: AC and BD.
ABCD = BCDA = DCBA, but ABDC is different.
No three points on a line, so there are true corners.
traps: Don't confuse a side with a diagonal.
Not every order of letters names the same figure.
Opposite angles are not adjacent angles.

learn.hook: An arrowhead has four sides, but one of its corners points inwards. Is it still a quadrilateral? Yes, a non-convex one!
points: Convex quadrilateral: every interior angle is less than 180° and the two diagonals cross inside it.
Non-convex (concave) quadrilateral: one interior angle is a reflex angle (more than 180°), like an arrowhead; one diagonal lies outside.
The interior angle at a vertex is the angle inside the figure; at the 'dent' of an arrowhead it is reflex. The four interior angles of any simple quadrilateral still add to 360°.

Other four-sided figures: self-intersecting (like a bow-tie, where two sides cross) and non-planar (the four points are not all in one plane, like a bent frame). A Venn diagram of 4-gons puts convex and non-convex quadrilaterals inside the bigger family of 4-gons.

example.q: An arrowhead quadrilateral has angles 30°, 40° and 30° at three vertices. Find the fourth angle and say what kind it is.

learn.reallife: The arrowhead shape is common in road signs and kites; its reflex angle points inwards.

games.title: 4-gon facts
items: In a convex quadrilateral both diagonals lie inside.
They cross inside the figure.
A non-convex quadrilateral has an angle greater than 180°.
That reflex angle makes the dent.
A bow-tie is a quadrilateral in the usual sense.
Its sides cross, so it is self-intersecting.
The interior angles of an arrowhead add to 360°.
Like every simple quadrilateral.
Four points not in one plane can still form a flat quadrilateral.
That 4-gon is non-planar.

quiz.q: A quadrilateral has angles 85°, 95°, 70° and 110°. Is it convex?
options: Yes, all angles are less than 180°
No, it has a reflex angle
No, the angles do not add to 360°
quiz.explain: Every angle is below 180°.
steps: Answer: Yes, all angles are less than 180°
quiz.mistake: Thinks an obtuse angle makes it non-convex

quiz.q: Three angles of a non-convex quadrilateral are 25°, 35° and 20°. What is the reflex angle?
steps: Angles of a quadrilateral add to 360°.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts from 180°

quiz.q: In a non-convex quadrilateral, how many interior angles can be reflex?
quiz.explain: The four angles add to 360°, so two reflex angles (each > 180°) are impossible.
steps: Two reflex angles would add to more than 360°.
But all four angles add to exactly 360°.
So only one angle can be reflex.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any number is possible

quiz.q: Where do the diagonals of a convex quadrilateral meet?
quiz.explain: In a convex quadrilateral the diagonals cross inside.
steps: In a convex quadrilateral both diagonals lie inside.
So they cross inside the quadrilateral.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up with the non-convex case

quiz.q: Which figure is self-intersecting?
options: A bow-tie whose two sides cross
quiz.explain: Two of its sides cross each other at a point that is not a vertex.
steps: Self-intersecting means two sides cross at a point that is not a vertex.
A bow-tie has two crossing sides.
An arrowhead is non-convex, not self-intersecting.
Answer: A bow-tie whose two sides cross
quiz.mistake: Thinks a non-convex shape is self-intersecting

quiz.q: A 4-gon whose four vertices are not all in one plane is called:
quiz.explain: Its vertices do not lie on one flat surface.
steps: A 4-gon whose vertices are not all on one flat surface is non-planar.
quiz.mistake: Confuses with concave

quiz.q: In an arrowhead ABCD with the dent at C, what kind of angle is the interior angle at C?
quiz.explain: At the dent the inside angle is more than 180°.
steps: At the dent of an arrowhead, the inside angle is more than 180°.
quiz.mistake: Measures the outside angle instead

quiz.q: Which statement fits a Venn diagram of 4-gons?
options: Convex quadrilaterals are a subset of all quadrilaterals, which are a subset of 4-gons
quiz.explain: 4-gons include quadrilaterals (simple, planar) and other types like bow-ties and non-planar figures.
steps: 4-gons include quadrilaterals plus bow-ties and non-planar figures.
Convex quadrilaterals are some of the quadrilaterals.
Answer: Convex quadrilaterals are a subset of all quadrilaterals, which are a subset of 4-gons
quiz.mistake: Thinks all four-sided figures are convex

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How can I tell if a quadrilateral is convex?"
teach.praise: Brilliant! Convex means all angles are under 180° and the diagonals cross inside!
teach.nudge: What size must every angle be? Where do the diagonals meet?

revise.summary: A convex quadrilateral has all angles under 180° and diagonals crossing inside. A non-convex one has exactly one reflex angle. Other 4-gons are self-intersecting (bow-ties) or non-planar.
focus: Classify quadrilaterals as convex or non-convex.
Find a reflex angle from the other three.
Place 4-gons in a Venn diagram.
remember: Interior angles of a simple quadrilateral add to 360°.
Only one angle can be reflex.
traps: An obtuse angle does not make it non-convex.
Subtract from 360°, not 180°.
A non-convex shape is not self-intersecting.

learn.hook: Four sticks joined at the ends with pins can wiggle into many shapes. Engineers use this to build machines!
points: A four-bar linkage is a quadrilateral with fixed side lengths but movable joints; its angles change as it moves. It powers windscreen wipers, bicycle pedals with legs, and folding chairs.

Parallelogram linkages keep opposite sides parallel while moving: Watt's parallel motion guided steam-engine pistons; a pantograph copies a drawing larger or smaller; forces combine by the parallelogram rule.
Given 4 points with no three in a line, they can be joined into 3 different 4-gons (the vertex orders ABCD, ABDC, ACBD).

If the 4 points are corners of a convex shape, you get 1 convex quadrilateral and 2 self-intersecting 4-gons. If one point is inside the triangle of the other three, you get 3 non-convex quadrilaterals.

example.q: Points A(0, 0), B(4, 0), C(4, 3), D(0, 3). How many 4-gons can be formed and of which kinds?
steps: The points form a rectangle, so they are in convex position
Order ABCD gives the convex rectangle
Orders ABDC and ACBD give bow-ties

learn.reallife: Architects and artists once used pantographs to enlarge drawings; today some trains use a pantograph to touch the overhead wire.

games.title: Linkage use
pairs: Copies a drawing at a different size
Guides a piston in a straight line

games.title: 4 points: what can you get?
items: Convex position: 1 convex + 2 bow-ties
One point inside: 3 non-convex
Convex position: 3 convex quadrilaterals
One point inside: a bow-tie
4 points give 3 different 4-gons in all

quiz.q: In a four-bar linkage, what stays fixed as it moves?
options: The lengths of the four bars
quiz.explain: The joints turn, so angles and diagonals change but bar lengths do not.
steps: In a four-bar linkage, the joints turn.
Angles, diagonals and area change; the bar lengths do not.
Answer: The lengths of the four bars
quiz.mistake: Thinks the shape is rigid

quiz.q: A rhombus-shaped linkage of 4 equal bars is pushed. Which shape can it NOT become?
options: A rectangle that is not a square
quiz.explain: All sides stay equal, so it is always a rhombus (a square at one moment), never a non-square rectangle.
steps: All four bars stay equal, so it is always a rhombus.
At one moment it is a square, but never a rectangle with unequal sides.
Answer: A rectangle that is not a square
quiz.mistake: Forgets that side lengths are fixed

quiz.q: What does a pantograph do?
options: Copies a drawing at a larger or smaller size
quiz.explain: Its parallelogram linkage keeps the copy similar to the original.
steps: A pantograph uses a parallelogram linkage.
It copies a drawing at a larger or smaller size, keeping it similar.
Answer: Copies a drawing at a larger or smaller size
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with a protractor

quiz.q: Four points have no three in a line. How many different 4-gons can be formed using all four as vertices?
quiz.explain: The orders ABCD, ABDC and ACBD give the only distinct figures.
steps: Distinct 4-gons come from the vertex orders ABCD, ABDC, ACBD.
Other orderings repeat these (by starting point or direction).
quiz.mistake: Counts all 24 orderings

quiz.q: Four points form a convex shape. How many of the 4-gons are self-intersecting?
quiz.explain: Only one ordering goes round the outside; the other two make bow-ties.
steps: In convex position, only one ordering goes round the outside (convex).
The other two orderings make bow-ties.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all are convex

quiz.q: Point D is inside triangle ABC. How many non-convex quadrilaterals can be formed with A, B, C, D as vertices?
quiz.explain: Each choice of where to insert D between two of A, B, C gives an arrowhead.
steps: With D inside triangle ABC, D can be inserted between any two of A, B, C.
Each choice gives an arrowhead: 3 non-convex quadrilaterals.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a point inside gives a bow-tie

quiz.q: Two forces act on a box along two sides of a parallelogram. By the parallelogram rule, the combined force is shown by:
options: the diagonal from the common corner
quiz.explain: The resultant is the diagonal of the parallelogram formed by the two forces.
steps: Parallelogram rule: the two forces are adjacent sides.
The combined force is the diagonal from their common corner.
Answer: the diagonal from the common corner
quiz.mistake: Adds the lengths of the sides

quiz.q: Which mechanism helped steam engines move a piston rod in a nearly straight line?
quiz.explain: James Watt designed a linkage using a parallelogram for this.
steps: James Watt designed a linkage to guide a piston rod nearly straight.
It is called Watt's parallel motion.
quiz.mistake: Names an unrelated machine

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "I have four points. How many different four-sided figures can I make?"
teach.praise: Exactly! Three ways to join them; what you get depends on whether the points are in convex position!
teach.nudge: How many different orders are there? Does it matter if a point is inside the others?

revise.summary: A four-bar linkage has fixed bar lengths but moving joints; parallelogram linkages drive pantographs and Watt's parallel motion. Four points can be joined into 3 different 4-gons.
focus: Explain how linkages move.
Count 4-gons on four points.
Use the parallelogram rule for forces.
remember: One point inside the triangle: 3 non-convex quadrilaterals.
Resultant force = diagonal from the common corner.
traps: A linkage is not rigid: angles change.
Don't count all 24 orderings.
An equal-bar linkage stays a rhombus.

learn.hook: Kites in the Makar Sankranti sky, carrom boards and window panes are all quadrilaterals, but they belong to different branches of one big family!
points: A quadrilateral has 4 sides, 4 angles, 4 vertices and 2 diagonals. Its interior angles always add up to 360°, because a diagonal splits it into two triangles.
Trapezium: a pair of opposite sides parallel. Parallelogram: both pairs of opposite sides parallel.
Rectangle: a parallelogram with all angles 90°. Rhombus: a parallelogram with all sides equal. Square: both a rectangle and a rhombus.
Kite: two pairs of equal adjacent sides; its diagonals are perpendicular.
So every square is a rectangle and a rhombus, and every rectangle and rhombus is a parallelogram, but not the other way round.

example.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are x, x + 10°, x + 20° and x + 30°. Find all four angles.

learn.reallife: Engineers use parallelogram shapes in car jacks and folding gates, because they can change shape while opposite sides stay parallel.

games.title: Family facts
items: Every square is a rhombus
A square has all four sides equal, which is what a rhombus needs.
Every rhombus is a square
A rhombus can have angles like 60° and 120°, so it need not be a square.
Every rectangle is a parallelogram
A rectangle has both pairs of opposite sides parallel.
A square is a parallelogram
Both pairs of opposite sides of a square are parallel.
The angles of any quadrilateral add up to 180°
They add up to 360°: a diagonal makes two triangles of 180° each.
The diagonals of a kite are perpendicular
The long diagonal of a kite is a line of symmetry that cuts the other diagonal at right angles.

games.title: Name the quadrilateral
pairs: Both pairs of opposite sides parallel
Two pairs of equal adjacent sides

quiz.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 80°, 95° and 110°. What is the fourth angle?
quiz.explain: The angles add up to 360°, so the fourth angle is 360° − (80° + 95° + 110°) = 360° − 285° = 75°.
quiz.mistake: Uses 180° or makes an addition slip

quiz.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 : 4. What is the largest angle?
quiz.explain: There are 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10 parts, so one part is 36°. The largest angle is 4 × 36° = 144°.
quiz.mistake: Divides 180° instead of 360° into the parts, getting 72°

quiz.q: Which statement is always true?
quiz.explain: A square has four equal sides, so it is a special rhombus. The others are true only sometimes.
steps: A square has four equal sides, so it is a rhombus.
A rhombus or rectangle need not be a square; a trapezium need not be a parallelogram.
Answer: Every square is a rhombus
quiz.mistake: Reverses the family tree: a square is a rhombus, but a rhombus need not be a square

quiz.q: A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides. What is it?
quiz.explain: A quadrilateral with only one pair of parallel sides is a trapezium. Parallelograms and rhombuses have two pairs.
steps: Exactly one pair of parallel sides defines a trapezium.
Parallelograms and rhombuses have two pairs.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any shape with parallel sides is a parallelogram

quiz.q: Which quadrilateral has two pairs of equal adjacent sides and diagonals that cross at right angles, but need not have parallel sides?
quiz.explain: That is a kite, like the ones flown on Makar Sankranti.
steps: Two pairs of equal adjacent sides and perpendicular diagonals: a kite.
A kite need not have parallel sides.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a kite with a rhombus or parallelogram

quiz.q: A rhombus has equal diagonals. What special quadrilateral is it?
quiz.explain: A parallelogram with equal diagonals is a rectangle. A rhombus that is also a rectangle is a square.
steps: A parallelogram with equal diagonals is a rectangle.
A rhombus that is also a rectangle is a square.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the diagonals of a rhombus can never be equal

quiz.q: What is the sum of the exterior angles of a convex quadrilateral, taking one at each vertex?
quiz.explain: Walking once round any convex polygon you turn through one full turn, 360°.
quiz.mistake: Confuses exterior angles with the sum of interior angles of a triangle

quiz.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are x, x + 10°, x + 20° and x + 30°. What is the largest angle?
quiz.explain: 4x + 60° = 360°, so x = 75°. The largest angle is x + 30° = 105°.
quiz.mistake: Gives x (75°) instead of the largest angle

teach.ask: Gappu is puzzled: "My teacher says a square is a rectangle. But they have different names! How can that be?"
teach.praise: A rectangle just needs four right angles and opposite sides equal and parallel. A square has all that, so it is a special kind of rectangle!
teach.nudge: What does a shape need to be called a rectangle? Does a square have those things?

revise.summary: A quadrilateral's angles add to 360°. Trapeziums, parallelograms, rectangles, rhombuses, squares and kites form a family: every square is a rectangle and a rhombus, and these are parallelograms.
focus: Use the angle sum of 360°.
Know the definitions of each quadrilateral.
Place shapes in the family tree.
remember: Kite: two pairs of equal adjacent sides; diagonals perpendicular.
traps: A rhombus need not be a square.
A trapezium is not a parallelogram.

learn.hook: Push the top of a folding gate sideways: it leans, but opposite sides stay equal and parallel. That's the parallelogram's superpower!
points: A diagonal divides a parallelogram into two congruent triangles.
In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal and opposite angles are equal.
Adjacent angles are supplementary: they add up to 180° (co-interior angles between parallel lines).
The diagonals bisect each other: they cut each other into two equal halves.

A quadrilateral is a parallelogram if any one of these holds: both pairs of opposite sides equal, both pairs of opposite angles equal, diagonals bisect each other, or one pair of opposite sides is both equal and parallel. In a rectangle the diagonals are also equal; in a rhombus they are also perpendicular.

example.q: In parallelogram PQRS, ∠P = 65°. Find the other three angles.

learn.reallife: Table lamps with folding arms, the scissor lift used by electricians and many bridge frames rely on parallelogram properties.

quiz.q: One angle of a parallelogram is 70°. What is the size of an angle next to it?
quiz.explain: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram are supplementary: 180° − 70° = 110°.
steps: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram are supplementary.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all angles of a parallelogram are equal, or subtracts from 90°

quiz.q: In parallelogram ABCD the diagonals meet at O, and AC = 16 cm. What is AO?
quiz.explain: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so AO = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm.
steps: Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that bisect means cut into two equal halves

quiz.q: A parallelogram has sides 9 cm and 6 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: Opposite sides are equal, so the perimeter is 2 × (9 + 6) = 30 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds only two sides, or multiplies the sides

quiz.q: Two opposite angles of a parallelogram are (3x − 10)° and (2x + 20)°. What is the size of each of these angles?
quiz.explain: Opposite angles are equal: 3x − 10 = 2x + 20, so x = 30. Each angle is 3 × 30 − 10 = 80°.
quiz.mistake: Gives x (30) as the angle, or uses supplementary angles by mistake

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT always true for a parallelogram?
quiz.explain: Equal diagonals happen only when the parallelogram is a rectangle (or square).
steps: Opposite sides equal, opposite angles equal, diagonals bisect: always true.
Equal diagonals happen only for rectangles (and squares).
quiz.mistake: Assumes rectangle properties hold for every parallelogram

quiz.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 12 cm and 16 cm. What is the length of each side?
quiz.explain: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making right triangles with legs 6 cm and 8 cm. Side = √(36 + 64) = 10 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses the whole diagonals instead of their halves, getting 20 cm

quiz.q: Which condition guarantees that a quadrilateral is a parallelogram?
options: One pair of opposite sides is equal
One pair of opposite sides is both equal and parallel
quiz.explain: If one pair of opposite sides is equal AND parallel, the quadrilateral must be a parallelogram. Just equal is not enough: an isosceles trapezium has one pair of equal opposite sides.
steps: One pair of opposite sides both equal and parallel guarantees a parallelogram.
Only equal is not enough (isosceles trapezium); perpendicular diagonals or one right angle are not enough.
Answer: One pair of opposite sides is both equal and parallel
quiz.mistake: Thinks one pair of equal sides is enough

quiz.q: Two adjacent angles of a parallelogram are in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the smaller angle?
quiz.explain: Adjacent angles add to 180°. 180° ÷ 5 = 36°, so the angles are 72° and 108°.
quiz.mistake: Divides 360° into the parts as if they were all four angles

teach.ask: Gappu draws a slanted four-sided shape: "How can I be sure this is a parallelogram, and what do I get for free if it is?"
teach.praise: If both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, then opposite sides and angles are equal, and the diagonals bisect each other. So many free facts!
teach.nudge: What can you say about the opposite sides? And what happens where the diagonals cross?

revise.summary: In a parallelogram, opposite sides and opposite angles are equal, adjacent angles add to 180°, and the diagonals bisect each other.
focus: Find angles and sides of parallelograms.
Use bisecting diagonals.
Know the conditions that prove a parallelogram.
remember: One pair of opposite sides equal AND parallel is enough.
traps: Diagonals are equal only in rectangles.
One pair of equal sides is not enough.
Adjacent angles are supplementary, not equal.

topics.title: Proving a quadrilateral is a parallelogram

learn.hook: Measure only the sides, or only the diagonals, and still be sure it's a parallelogram? Yes, with the right converse!
points: If both pairs of opposite sides are equal, the quadrilateral is a parallelogram. Proof: diagonal AC gives △ABC ≅ △CDA (SSS), so alternate angles are equal and the sides are parallel.
If the diagonals bisect each other, it is a parallelogram. Proof: with diagonals meeting at O, △AOB ≅ △COD (SAS, vertically opposite angles), so ∠OAB = ∠OCD and AB ∥ CD; similarly AD ∥ BC.
If one pair of opposite sides is both equal and parallel, it is a parallelogram (△ABC ≅ △CDA by SAS).
Proofs use congruence rules SSS, SAS, ASA and then CPCT (corresponding parts of congruent triangles are equal).

example.q: In quadrilateral PQRS, diagonals meet at O with PO = 5, OR = 5, QO = 7, OS = 7. What is PQRS?
steps: O is the midpoint of PR (5 = 5)
O is the midpoint of QS (7 = 7)

learn.reallife: A carpenter checking a door frame can measure diagonals: if they bisect each other the frame is a parallelogram.

quiz.explain: Both pairs of opposite sides are equal.

topics.title: Rhombus, rectangle and square: special conditions

learn.hook: Draw the four angle bisectors of any parallelogram and, like magic, they box in a rectangle!
points: If a diagonal of a parallelogram bisects one of its angles, the parallelogram is a rhombus (the diagonal makes an isosceles triangle, so adjacent sides are equal).
The bisectors of the four angles of a parallelogram form a rectangle: adjacent angles add to 180°, so their halves add to 90°, and each corner of the inner figure is a right angle.

Converses with extra conditions: a parallelogram with equal diagonals is a rectangle; a parallelogram with perpendicular diagonals is a rhombus; a parallelogram with equal and perpendicular diagonals is a square.
Without 'parallelogram' these fail: a kite has perpendicular diagonals but is not a rhombus; an isosceles trapezium has equal diagonals but is not a rectangle.

example.q: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 110°. The bisectors of ∠A and ∠B meet at P. Find ∠APB.

learn.hook: Join the middles of two sides of any triangle and something magical appears: a line exactly parallel to the third side and exactly half as long!
points: Mid-point theorem: the segment joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and is half of it.
If D and E are mid-points of AB and AC in triangle ABC, then DE ∥ BC and DE = ½ BC.
Converse: a line through the mid-point of one side of a triangle, parallel to another side, bisects the third side.
Joining the mid-points of the three sides makes 4 congruent triangles, each with ¼ of the area of the original.
Joining the mid-points of the sides of ANY quadrilateral, in order, always gives a parallelogram.

example.q: In triangle ABC, AB = 8 cm, BC = 10 cm and CA = 12 cm. D, E and F are the mid-points of AB, BC and CA. Find the perimeter of triangle DEF.
steps: By the mid-point theorem, each side of DEF is half of a side of ABC
DE = ½ CA = 6, EF = ½ AB = 4, FD = ½ BC = 5

learn.reallife: Carpenters use the mid-point idea to fix a cross-bar exactly halfway up a triangular roof frame, knowing it will be level and half the width of the base.

topics.title: Midpoint theorem: proof, trapeziums and equal parts

learn.hook: Split a ladder into equal steps using just parallel lines. The midpoint theorem's big brother does it!
points: Proof of the midpoint theorem by construction: with D, E midpoints of AB, AC, extend DE to F with EF = DE. △ADE ≅ △CFE (SAS), so CF = AD = DB and CF ∥ AB. So DBCF is a parallelogram, giving DE ∥ BC and DF = BC, so DE = ½ BC.
Trapezium mid-segment: the segment joining the midpoints of the non-parallel sides is parallel to the bases and equals half their sum: (a + b)/2.
If three or more parallel lines cut equal parts on one transversal, they cut equal parts on every transversal.
To divide AB in a ratio like 3 : 5, draw a ray from A, mark 8 equal steps, join the 8th mark to B, and draw parallels through the other marks; the 3rd one meets AB at the dividing point.

learn.hook: Balance a cardboard triangle on a pencil tip. The balancing point is where the three medians meet!
points: A median joins a vertex of a triangle to the midpoint of the opposite side. Every triangle has three medians.
The three medians are concurrent: they meet at one point G, the centroid (the balancing point).
Centroid theorem: G divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1 from the vertex, so AG = ⅔ AD and GD = ⅓ AD. (Proof idea: join the midpoints of two sides and use the midpoint theorem.)
Trisecting a segment AD: make AD a median of some triangle (pick B, extend BD to C with DC = BD). The centroid G is at one-third from D; the midpoint of AG gives the other trisection point.

topics.title: Varignon shapes and tiling with any quadrilateral

learn.hook: Even a lopsided, wonky quadrilateral can tile a whole floor. Spin it around its edge midpoints and watch!
points: Varignon parallelogram (midpoints of the sides joined in order): its sides are parallel to the diagonals and half as long.
If the original's diagonals are perpendicular, the Varignon figure is a rectangle; if they are equal, it is a rhombus; if they are equal and perpendicular, a square.

Tiling method 1: rotate a copy of the quadrilateral by 180° about the midpoint of one edge; keep doing this about edge midpoints. The four angles (sum 360°) meet at every vertex, and copies fill the plane.
Tiling method 2: the Varignon parallelograms of copies form a parallelogram grid, which shows how translated copies of the quadrilateral fit together.

example.q: A quadrilateral has diagonals 10 cm and 14 cm that are perpendicular. Describe its Varignon figure and its perimeter.
steps: Sides are half the diagonals: 5 cm and 7 cm
example.answer: A 5 cm by 7 cm rectangle, perimeter 24 cm

learn.reallife: Tile designers use 180° rotations about edge midpoints to make floor patterns with irregular shapes.

topics.title: Which shapes tile? Pentagons, hats and bow-ties

learn.hook: Bathroom tiles are squares, honeycombs are hexagons, but you'll never see a floor of regular pentagons. Why?
points: Any triangle and any quadrilateral (even a non-convex one) can tile the plane.
A regular pentagon cannot: each angle is 108°, and 360 ÷ 108 is not a whole number, so copies cannot fill the space around a point.
Aperiodic tilings cover the plane but never repeat in a regular pattern. In 2023 a single shape nicknamed the 'hat' was found that tiles the plane only aperiodically.
Scissors congruence: a shape can be cut into pieces and rearranged. For example, joining the midpoints of a triangle's sides cuts it into 4 congruent triangles.
In a self-intersecting (bow-tie) 4-gon, the four vertex angles add up to less than 360°: they are 360° − 2θ, where θ is the angle where the sides cross.

example.q: Can regular hexagons tile the plane? Regular pentagons?
steps: Hexagon angle = 120°; 360 ÷ 120 = 3: yes, three meet at a point
So hexagons tile; pentagons do not

learn.reallife: Honeybees build hexagonal cells because hexagons tile without gaps and use little wax.
